function.arguments: {"observation": "Deduplication was performed before removing rows with `biomarker_baseline = -999`, which means that a patient whose latest (highest `sample_seq`) row has a sentinel value in `biomarker_baseline` is excluded even if an earlier row for the same patient had a valid baseline value. This could bias the average change if such patients are systematically different (e.g., those who failed QC on the final test had worse baseline disease).", "implication": "The order of operations matters. To preserve valid baseline values from earlier samples, we must first identify and retain valid baseline rows (i.e., non -999) before deduplication. The correct sequence is: (1) filter out rows with `biomarker_baseline == -999` only for the purpose of baseline validity; (2) deduplicate on `patient_id` using the highest `sample_seq`, but only among rows where `biomarker_baseline` is valid. Otherwise, we risk discarding patients who had valid data in earlier assays."}
function.name: note_finding
